title: Faint cover subtitle remains a reading question
place: cover, faint subtitle
body: The cover supplies the label “Vrai groupe fondamental,” but the frozen subtitle remains uncertain. Hua's contextual “[feuilles anciennes]” differs from the audited alternatives and should be recorded as a question, not used to replace the frozen reading or to date the manuscript sheets.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Les « feuilles anciennes » : représentabilité et recollement” opening, Hua pp.130–134 → scans131–135; backward reference to the scan124 cover, whose Hua page is123.

title: The two awkward hypotheses are expressly provisional
place: typescript p.2, provisional conditions (v) and (vi)
body: The source explicitly marks (v), the infinitesimal/separable decomposition, and (vi), reducedness of S, as provisional assumptions serving the rigidity lemma. This supports Hua's account of a construction with restricted hypotheses and prevents the source from being cited here as an unconditional existence theorem over every base; assumptions (i)–(iv) enter this selected witness only by reference and are supplied in Hua's context from the preceding letter page.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Le dispositif”, Hua pp.124–126 → scans125–127; source witness Hua p.125 → scan126. Scans125 and127 are outside supplied evidence.

title: The perfect-field splitting is a semidirect product
place: typescript p.2, perfect-field decomposition paragraph
body: The perfect-field remark identifies the reduced subgroup with the separable quotient but immediately retains its action on the infinitesimal part. Any summary as a direct product would lose the source's explicit qualification; the result recorded here is a semidirect decomposition under the stated perfect-field hypothesis.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Le dispositif” and “Le dévissage sur un corps parfait”, Hua pp.124–126 → scans125–127; supplied source Hua p.125 → scan126. Scans125 and127 are outside supplied evidence.

title: Rigidity is used to pass to an exact functor of isomorphism classes
place: typescript p.2, rigidity lemma and pointed-torsor functor diagrams
source_words: “alors u=v”; “exactitude de F, et du lemme”.
body: The page defines Z(G) as the set of isomorphism classes of pointed F(G)-torsors and asserts compatibility with products and equalizers by exactness of F and the rigidity lemma. It supports the torsor-based route in Hua's finding, while the categorical closure and exactness assumptions must remain attached; the later unrestricted category of all admissible S-groups is not automatically interchangeable with this setting. Isomorphism classes can still form a set when objects have automorphisms, so rigidity supports the exactness/descent argument rather than the mere existence of that set; Hua's stronger set-versus-groupoid wording should not be repeated.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Le foncteur, et ce qu’il vérifie” and “La pro-représentabilité”, Hua pp.124–126 → scans125–127; supplied witness Hua p.125 → scan126. Scans125 and127 are outside supplied evidence.

title: The homotopy sequence is a conjecture, including its local-group formulation
place: typescript p.5, opening paragraph and revisions
source_words: deleted “hypothèse”, inserted “conjecture”; “reliés par une suite exacte”.
body: The revision from “hypothèse” to “conjecture” fixes the status of the proposed sequence relating the relative group object, the local system of fundamental groups on X, and the inverse image of the analogous object on Y. The absence of a base field is explicitly said to make the formulation unclear, and the cancelled continuation about sections and a complete local base should not be promoted into a surviving theorem.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “La suite exacte d’homotopie, à trouver”, Hua pp.127–129 → scans128–130, especially Hua p.128 → scan129. Scan128 is outside supplied evidence.

title: The product formula is conditional and concerns the total group scheme
place: typescript p.5, conditional product formula
body: The product identity for complete X,Y over an algebraically closed k is introduced as a consequence the conjecture would imply. Hua rightly distinguishes its total group scheme, including infinitesimal structure, from the prime-to-characteristic assertion elsewhere in his reading; this leaf does not provide a proof of the product identity or evidence for the chronology of that comparison.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “La suite exacte d’homotopie, à trouver”, Hua p.128 → scan129; contextual comparison with Hua p.62 → scan63, outside supplied evidence.

title: The abelian-variety formula is written explicitly, but the local derivation is conditional
place: typescript p.5, abelian-variety computation and Cartier duality
source_words: “Utilisant tes raisonnements”; “On en déduit”; “avec sa partie infinitésimale aussi”.
body: The source writes Π₁(X/k)=lim←ₙ X[n], gives transition X[mn]→X[n] as multiplication by m, and identifies its Cartier dual with lim→ₙ X*[n]. It connects this to commutativity and minimal torsors being isogenous abelian varieties, but the visible chain follows the conjectural product formula and invokes the correspondent's arguments, so this page supplies an explicit announced computation rather than a self-contained independent proof.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Le calcul sur une variété abélienne”, Hua p.128 within pp.127–129 → supplied scan129.

title: The Witt-module paragraph records an expectation, not a specified equivalence
place: typescript p.5 ending and p.6 opening, Witt expectation and family variation
source_words: “Il est hors de doute”; “Cartier doit l'avoir fait”; “devrait ... fournir”.
body: The proposed functor from infinitesimal commutative proalgebraic groups to Witt modules and its three-part decomposition are expressed as expectations, without a category equivalence, operators, or proof here. Scan130 continues with the anticipated uniform treatment of ℓ≠p and ℓ=p and variation in an abelian scheme, using the finite flat torsion kernels; those are programmatic benefits, not a completed construction on these pages.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Le calcul sur une variété abélienne”, Hua pp.128–129 → scans129–130.

title: The timetable does not independently date this continuation
place: typescript p.6, programme and unsigned closing
source_words: “Dans trois ans”; “Sauf difficultés imprévues”; “Bien à toi”.
body: The closing continuation gives a relative schedule for the fundamental group, categories, duality/intersection theory, Weil cohomology, and homotopy, but no date or signature on the selected witness. “18 août 1959” and Serre are contextual attributions from Hua's enclosing section, not independently read from scans126/129/130. The parent separately verified publisher metadata for Nori's 1976, 1982, and 1983 publications; that bibliographic verification does not independently date this letter continuation or establish a priority claim.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Le calendrier”, Hua p.129 → scan130, within the enclosing “Lettre à Serre, 18 août 1959” section, Hua pp.124–129 → scans125–130. title: Uniqueness of the infinitesimal kernel need not use reducedness under an explicit étale-quotient hypothesis
place: definition of admissible group, uniqueness question and margin
body: With two exact sequences having geometrically injective kernels Uᵢ and finite étale quotients Γᵢ over an arbitrary S, each composite U₁→G→Γ₂ lands in the identity section because its inverse image is clopen and contains every geometric point. Thus U₁⊂U₂ and conversely, so uniqueness does not require S reduced under these precise hypotheses; this answers the margin question about uniqueness and does not remove reducedness from the separate rigidity assertion.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Les groupes admissibles”, Hua p.136 → scan137.
reason: Independent clopen-preimage proof establishes equality of the two kernels over arbitrary S when the quotients are finite étale and the kernels geometrically injective; reducedness is unused.

title: The base-change direction has already been visibly corrected in the source
place: Proposition1, cancelled direction, inserted correction and reduced-base margin
source_words: “Si G ... est admissible”; “la réciproque ... fidèlement plat”; margin “S′ et S réduits”.
body: The frozen reading preserves a cancelled descending statement and an inserted forward base-change statement, followed by faithfully flat descent as the converse. Hua's final mathematical ordering agrees, but his footnote describes the reversed draft as what the page says; the visible insertion and the reduced-base margin are additional source evidence that the note should retain.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Les groupes admissibles”, Proposition1 and footnote, Hua p.136 → scan137.

title: The torsor hypothesis in rigidity must not disappear
place: Proposition3, inserted principal-torsor hypothesis
source_words: inserted “princ. sous G|principal sous G”; “admissible sur S ... réduit connexe”.
body: The source qualifies P as a principal torsor under an admissible group over reduced connected S. Hua's sentence about two sections of an arbitrary reduced connected P drops that hypothesis and is false: for S=Spec k[t], P=𝔸¹_S, the sections 0 and t agree at t=0 but differ globally; the corrected torsor-rigidity statement is separately justified under the finite-étale-quotient hypotheses in proof C.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Les groupes admissibles”, Proposition3, Hua p.137 → scan138.
reason: The explicit sections z=0 and z=t of A1 over Spec k[t] disprove the unqualified contextual version; a separate proof retains the source’s torsor/admissibility hypotheses.

title: Minimality requires a declared mathematical repair, not a transcription repair
place: final definition of minimal pointed torsor
body: The frozen definition writes P′ as relative to G and uses P′×_G G′; Hua replaces this by a G′-torsor extended through P′×_{G′}G. That is the mathematically intended reading used in the checks below, together with **proper** admissible subgroup, but these repairs must remain explicit because the source's literal formula and absence of an explicit strictness word are preserved in the transcription.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Minimalité” and its editorial footnote, Hua p.137 → scan138.

title: Gothic Z is contextual evidence, not a resolved glyph
place: definition notation and Proposition4 source and target
source_words: audited alternatives Z⁰|Z¹ in the definition; Z¹ in the proposition source; bare Z in its target.
body: Hua normalizes the old leaves to a gothic Z and identifies their functor with the letter's Z(S,a;G). This is useful as a contextual comparison, but it does not resolve the audited source alternatives or justify changing the source and target superscripts in the frozen transcription.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Minimalité”, Hua pp.137–138 → scans138–139; global notation convention at lines33–34 normalizes the symbol but supplies no independent glyph audit.

title: The minimality argument needs an admissible flat reduction
place: Proposition4 proof setup and opening fibre product
body: To infer u=v from minimality one must show that H=Eq(u,v) is an admissible finite flat subgroup and that R=P×_Q P′ is a pointed H-torsor yielding P by extension of structure group. The supplied face stops before either assertion, and neither follows merely from the existence of a scheme-theoretic fibre product; the counterexample below makes both flatness failures explicit.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “La proposition 4, démontrée deux fois”, Hua pp.138–140 → scans139–141; only Hua pp.138–139 → scans139–140 are supplied. Scan141 is outside supplied evidence.
reason: The conditional use of minimality requires an admissible flat subgroup reduction, and the explicit equalizer and cusp computations show why existence of the scheme fibre product alone is insufficient.

title: The supplied attempted proof stops; the contextual restart adds hypotheses
place: sole unfinished sentence ending with a comma
body: Our scan140 is Hua p.139 and ends at the introduction of R; Hua's restart at p.140 and completion at pp.141–142 are context-only scans141–143. His footnote says the restart introduces a category C closed under products, equalizers, and images, so the contextual completion cannot be silently imported into the earlier unrestricted admissible-group formulation or described as a proof visible on this supplied face.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “La proposition 4, démontrée deux fois” and “La fin de la proposition 4”, Hua pp.139–142 → scans140–143; only Hua p.139 → scan140 is supplied, while Hua pp.140–142 → scans141–143 are outside supplied evidence.

title: Reduced connectedness alone does not make all admissible-group equalizers flat
place: admissibility hypotheses and missing equalizer-flatness step
body: Over S=Spec k[t] in characteristic p, G=G′=α_p,S is admissible, while the equalizer of 0 and multiplication by t has coordinate algebra k[t,T]/(T^p,tT). Its generic fibre has length1 and its fibre at t=0 has length p, so it is not flat; closure under equalizers is a substantive extra condition even over a reduced connected regular base.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Les groupes admissibles” and “La proposition 4, démontrée deux fois”, Hua pp.136–140 → scans137–141; source witnesses Hua pp.136,138,139 → scans137,139,140, and scan141 is outside supplied evidence.
reason: The algebra k[t,T]/(T^p,tT) has generic fibre length1 and special fibre length p, proving nonflatness directly while both source groups are admissible.

title: A cusp gives a minimal pointed torsor for which the broad injectivity claim fails
place: intended minimality definition, claimed injectivity and unfinished fibre product
body: Let A=k[x,y]/(y^p−x^(p+1)) for an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, take the cusp point a:Spec k→Spec A, and point the α_p-torsor z^p=x by z=0. It is nontrivial and minimal among finite flat subgroup reductions, but the distinct endomorphisms 0 and [x] both push it to a pointed-trivial torsor because x^p·x=y^p; the resulting R is the nonflat normalization Spec k[z]→Spec A. This refutes the unrestricted intended assertion, while [x] is a variable S-group morphism and therefore is not a morphism of constant k-groups in the letter's example; the proposed equalizer-closed categorical restart also excludes the nonflat equalizer used here.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Minimalité” and “La proposition 4, démontrée deux fois”, Hua pp.137–140 → scans138–141; supplied witnesses are scans138–140, while the restart at scan141 is outside supplied evidence.
reason: Full algebraic proof establishes nontriviality, minimality among finite flat closed subgroup reductions, equality of pointed pushforwards, and the exact nonflat fibre product; the parent independently rechecked it. The refutation is explicitly limited to the repaired all-admissible-S-group formulation.

title: The contextual literature identification is not a new priority result
place: torsor functor, announced computation and unsigned letter continuation
body: These witnesses support the pointed-torsor method, explicit infinitesimal part, and stated abelian-variety formula recorded in Hua's finding. His literature identification and date attribution remain credited context, while the source-dependent hypotheses, conjectural step, and unfinished unrestricted proof prevent an unqualified priority or full-generality claim from this package.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote 29, “Ce que c’est, aujourd’hui”, Hua pp.127–129 → scans128–130; scan128 is outside supplied evidence. Also context/notes/RESULTS_STATE.md, Hua findings register 29-fundamental-group-scheme-via-torsors.

title: Relation to the registered group-scheme work is limited and precise
place: scope of finite-flat admissible-group claims
body: The finite admissible-group and pointed-torsor arguments do not settle LM1 E.11's general separated locally finitely presented group-scheme question or re-prove LM1 E.2's characteristic-zero linear exponential assertion. The positive-characteristic cusp check addresses the local minimality claim alone; N063's cancelled descent/rank discussion and N100's Weyl-subquotient test remain separate first-pass leads, with no direct mathematical implication established by these leaves.
